false_positives.candidate:
Recovery codes are handed to user storage in plaintext

Handing raw secrets to a user-storage CredentialInputUpdater is how the SPI already works: passwords reach updateCredential in plaintext too, and the provider decides how to store them (the same test provider hashes the raw password it gets). Login also sends the raw code to isValid (RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator:72), so the provider has to handle raw input either way. Whether codes end up stored in cleartext is the provider's choice, not something this change forces; only the in-tree test fixture stores them raw.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Unsafe raw List deserialization without type safety. Calling Optional.get() directly on the Optional returned by RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user) without checking isPresent() can lead to a NoSuchElementException if the Optional is empty.

After creating the RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel, consider setting its id from the stored credential (e.g., myUser.recoveryCodes.getId()); otherwise getId() will be null and downstream removal by id (e.g., removeStoredCredentialById in the authenticator flow) may not work.

false_positives.candidate:
Strategy cases enable rolling-updates on an image that may not have it built in

The operator adds `--optimized` only when a custom image is configured or start-optimized is set, and start-optimized defaults to false. With the stock image the server runs a build on startup, so `--features=rolling-updates` takes effect and the start does not fail. With the custom image, the feature is already built in.

Need to add changelog/release notes documenting the exit code change and migration guidance

false_positives.candidate:
With both admin FGAP flags on, V2 group-permission methods throw; group deletion and the management-permissions endpoints break

V1 and V2 cannot both be enabled. ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ and ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 share the unversioned key admin-fine-grained-authz. Profile.configure throws if both versions are enabled explicitly, and it marks only one version of each feature as enabled. So the listener and the GroupResource endpoints guarded by the V1 flag can never reach MgmtPermissionsV2.

false_negatives.golden_comment: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the permission fallback checks for both VIEW and MANAGE scopes (hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)), but canManage() should only grant access for MANAGE scope, not VIEW. This means users with only VIEW permission on groups can pass the canManage() check, granting them write access they should not have. The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.

In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, hasPermission is called with groupResource.getId() and the same groupResource.getId() is added to granted, but hasPermission resolves resources by name (treating the argument as a group id) and the GroupPermissionEvaluator contract says this method returns group IDs that are later used as UserModel.GROUPS and in getUsersCount group filters. This mismatch means per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions may not yield the expected group IDs for filtering and counts, and evaluation may effectively only look at the type-level 'all-groups' resource; consider revisiting whether this should operate on the underlying group ids (resource names) instead so it aligns with the JPA queries and the interface contract.

false_positives.candidate:
Password step of username-first flows now renders passkey UI after a wrong password

PasswordForm overrides createLoginForm to render login-password.ftl (PasswordForm.java:66-67). That template never imports passkeys.ftl; only login.ftl and login-username.ftl call conditionalUIData. Setting the attributes therefore puts no passkey UI on the password page.

false_negatives.golden_comment: In UsernameForm.authenticate(), isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is called without passing the required UserModel parameter.

With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login. Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.

false_positives.candidate:
New 'NEVER DO' hasattr rule has a misleading example and conflicts with existing usage

The entry follows the section's existing 'WRONG: <thing to avoid>' format (for example, line 435), so the heading clearly marks hasattr-for-union-narrowing as the anti-pattern. Its purpose is type narrowing, not runtime correctness. The raw count of 226 `hasattr(` calls does not show any conflict, because the rule only covers narrowing unions and the finding does not show that those calls do that.

false_negatives.golden_comment: In the SpanFlusher flush loop, metric tags inconsistently use 'shard' (e.g., in spans.buffer.flusher.produce and spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes) and 'shards' (in spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce) for the same shard identifier value. This prevents correct metric aggregation across flush stages — dashboards and alerts filtering by tag 'shard' will miss data tagged as 'shards' and vice versa.
The test_basic function in test_consumer.py uses a monkeypatched time.sleep that returns immediately, but then calls time.sleep(0.1) expecting it to actually wait.

Because flusher processes are created via multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process, they are instances of multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess, which on POSIX is not a subclass of multiprocessing.Process, so this isinstance check will always be false and hung processes won't be killed here.
Sleep in test_consumer.py won’t actually wait because time.sleep was monkeypatched above; consider restoring sleep or using a different sync to ensure the flusher has time to process.

Breaking out of the loop when the deadline has elapsed can skip terminating remaining flusher processes, potentially leaving them running after shutdown; consider ensuring termination is attempted even if the deadline is exceeded.

true_positives.golden_comment: Wrong value `6` passed for `group_2` occurrence — the data packet specifies `"group_2": 10`. Should be `10` to accurately reflect the test scenario, which will ensure the test produces the correct occurrence data.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe builds its expected occurrence with the wrong group key

`IssueOccurrence` defines its own `__eq__`, which compares only `id`. The dataclass decorator does not replace an `__eq__` already defined in the class body. Both occurrences use the hardcoded id `eb4b0acf...`, and the `event_data` dicts do not depend on the group key, so the different fingerprints do not make the assertion fail.
true_positives.reasoning: The golden comment identifies that value `6` is incorrectly used for `group_2` when it should be `10`. The candidate also points out that `test_dedupe` builds its expected occurrence with 'the wrong group key', which is the same underlying issue. The candidate goes further to explain why this bug isn't caught (due to `__eq__` only comparing `id`), but it is fundamentally identifying the same problem: the expected occurrence has an incorrect group key value.

false_negatives.golden_comment: MetricAlertDetectorHandler inherits from StatefulDetectorHandler but only contains pass, failing to implement its required abstract methods: counter_names (property), get_dedupe_value(), get_group_key_values(), and build_occurrence_and_event_data(). This will cause a TypeError at runtime when the class is instantiated.
Docstring says this returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult, but the method now returns a dict keyed by DetectorGroupKey. Consider updating the docstring to match the new return type.

false_positives.candidate:
Create passes the same obj to storage and to the legacy goroutine, and the response may alias it

The only legacy store here (playlist legacyStorage.Create) only reads obj: it type-asserts it, converts it to a command, and returns a fresh object from s.Get. So the legacy goroutine does not mutate obj or the returned object.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The context is being created with d.Log instead of the log variable that was initialized with additional context values (name, kind, method). This means those values won't be propagated to the logging context.
In DualWriterMode3's DeleteCollection method, when a storage operation fails, recordStorageDuration is incorrectly called with recordLegacyDuration instead.
Inconsistency: using name instead of options.Kind for metrics recording differs from other methods.

false_positives.candidate:
Confirm wire regeneration after the ProvideAnonymousDeviceService signature change

wire_gen.go is not committed: .gitignore lists **/wire_gen.go, and it is generated at build time from wire.go. So no stale generated file can pass an AnonStore into the new signature. The ProvideAnonDBStore/AnonStore binding left in wire.go:374-375 is now unused, but that is cleanup, not a compile break.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Race condition: Multiple concurrent requests could pass the device count check simultaneously and create devices beyond the limit. Consider using a database transaction or lock.

Anonymous authentication now fails entirely if anonDeviceService.TagDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached. Previously, device tagging was asynchronous and non-blocking. This change prevents anonymous users from authenticating when the device limit is reached.
The updateDevice function returns ErrDeviceLimitReached when rowsAffected == 0, but zero affected rows means the device doesn't exist or falls outside the time window, not that a limit was reached.

Time window calculation inconsistency: Using device.UpdatedAt.UTC().Add(-anonymousDeviceExpiration) as the lower bound but device.UpdatedAt as the current time may not match the intended logic. Consider using time.Now().UTC() consistently.

The `tagDeviceUI` function populates the local cache with the device ID before the `CreateOrUpdateDevice` call. If `ErrDeviceLimitReached` is returned, the cache entry remains set, allowing subsequent requests to bypass the device limit until the cache expires after 29 minutes.

false_positives.candidate:
Public group members tab renders an empty list

The route has a model (the group), so Ember generates an ObjectController for it (ember.js generateControllerFactory picks 'object' when context is non-array). The route sets the group as the model, and findMembers sets `members` on the group, so `members` in the template is proxied to group.members and the rows render.

Remove link is shown on automatic groups

The template uses the keyword form `{{each member in members itemView=...}}`, and for that form Ember binds the item view's context to the parent's context (the admin-group controller), not to the item. So `automatic` resolves to the group's flag.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.

In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.

The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.

false_positives.candidate:
Is open-uri loaded in the process that runs retrieve_topic?

Loading the Jobs module (app/jobs/base.rb) runs require_dependency on every scheduled job, including poll_feed.rb, which requires open-uri. Any process that runs retrieve_topic has therefore already loaded open-uri.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')

false_positives.candidate:
Is an in-memory delegation credential ever shown with delegationCredentialId null?

In-memory delegation credentials are built with id -1 and delegatedToId set to the delegation credential's id. CalendarManager maps delegatedToId to delegationCredentialId, so canDisconnect is false for them.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The updateManyByCredentialId call uses an empty data object, which prevents Prisma's @updatedAt decorator from updating the updatedAt timestamp. This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.
logic: macOS-specific sed syntax with empty string after -i flag will fail on Linux systems

Throwing a generic Error for authentication failures results in a 500 response in tRPC. Instead, it should return a structured TRPCError with an appropriate code, such as FORBIDDEN, to accurately reflect the error type.
Date is formatted with hardcoded 'en-US' locale instead of using the user's locale from useLocale, which can lead to incorrect date representation for users in different locales.

false_positives.candidate:
The reserved-slot branch skips the new override and working-hours checks

The reserved-slot branch only further filters `availableTimeSlots`, and those slots have already passed the fixed-host filter (line 488) and the loose-host filter (line 513). Both earlier filters always pass `workingHours` and `dateOverrides`, so the override and working-hours rules apply whether or not any reservation exists. Only the inert `organizerTimeZone` argument is true, and that is cosmetic.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime

Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))
